consensus_summary: Primary symbolic meaning of fornication/whoredom is spiritual unfaithfulness to God (idolatry, apostasy, covenant breach), grounded in the marriage metaphor for the divine covenant; Israel/church personified as harlot. Literal sexual immorality is foundational but non-symbolic; secondary extensions include political alliances, corrupt religion, and imperial commerce.
book_summary: Spiritual unfaithfulness consisting in breaking covenant with God to pursue other gods and kingdoms; the out-of-covenant union itself constitutes the whoredom, distinct from mere physical sin.
consensus_core_identification: Spiritual/covenant unfaithfulness (idolatry/apostasy) depicted as marital infidelity or prostitution.
book_core_identification: Spiritual unfaithfulness as covenant-breaking union with other gods and kingdoms.
boundary_disagreement: None; both treat the core as covenant infidelity encompassing gods and political powers, while excluding pure physical sin as the symbolic referent.
rationale: Minimum cores are identical: both identify the symbolic referent as spiritual covenant unfaithfulness (not physical fornication). The book's phrasing ('other gods and kingdoms'; 'out-of-covenant union is itself the whoredom') is a compact restatement of the consensus primary meaning already illustrated by Hosea, Ezekiel, Jeremiah, Exodus, and Revelation. No narrowing, broadening, reclassification, or replacement of the central category occurs.
strongest_objection: None material; at most a quibble that the book is more concise and does not enumerate every secondary extension (political commerce, etc.) already treated as elaborations of the same core by consensus.
